transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-18 10:30 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO, TidalFlow), Priya (Head of Infra), Sam (ML Platform)

Summary: quick check-in against commitment, confirm APAC region plan, discuss whether to add 10% headroom for BlackSep promo period, and agree next steps for contract amendment and benchmark run.

Topics: commitment amendment, regional onboarding (EU/SG), dedicated vs hosted tier for burst, KMS/encryption, canary strategy for model rollouts, benchmark scope, pricing prorate.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, good morning — thanks for taking time. quick agenda: confirm the amended commit numbers, APAC region decision, and a short perf ask for derek to run.
[00:12] Alex: yep, thx. we are mostly on the legal side, want to make sure pricing/prorate is clear. priya will also confirm KMS and networking.
[00:20] Priya: hi, yeah, main constraint is we need private-control-plane for PCI-ish data — we discussed VPC peering last week, still evaluation but leaning private. question: if we pick private, does redwood still support the same latency SLOs?
[00:35] Derek: in practice yes — private has same runtime but network egress adds a bit. for APAC we see typical p50 ~55ms for hosted, private tends to add 10–25ms depending on peering. we can run a perf shard to show numbers.
[00:50] Sam: also want the math on cost impact for dedicated GPUs vs hosted when we do burst events; our peak token distribution is heavy on short prompts (avg 30–60 tokens) but tail long seqs for summarization.
[01:05] Maya: understood. high level: if you go dedicated reserved, unit cost per token drops but commit required; hosted is flexible but more variable cost. our recommendation previously was reserved capacity with a small hosted fallback for blacksep promo.
[01:20] Alex: can you recalc the numbers with a 10% headroom added and include sequence-length mix? last table felt optimistic for the tail.
[01:30] Derek: sure, i'll run micro-benchmarks with your sample set. do you have the prompt set?
[01:36] Sam: i have a sanitized sample, will drop 1k requests to you by EOD. sorry for the delay.
[01:44] Maya: ok that helps. priya, about KMS — you mentioned preference?
[01:48] Priya: prefer customer-managed keys, ideally AWS KMS but open to HSM if needed for compliance. audit log retention — we need at least 2 years for product telemetry, and separate S3 buckets for logs.
[02:05] Derek: we support customer KMS in private deployments, and audit logs can be delivered to your S3. little caveat: for on-prem HSM we need an integration window, adds ~3–4 weeks.
[02:20] Alex: what's the usual canary rollout cadence? we want graceful degradation and automatic fallback to smaller model if primary runs out of capacity.
[02:28] Derek: standard is canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% across 48h with automatic rollback thresholds on latency and error rate. we have model-variant fallback — e.g., high-quality quantized variant for burst. note: quantization changes token-level cost and sometimes output tone.
[02:48] Sam: any tool to detect quality regressions automatically? we need to tie rollback to fails on our evals.
[02:55] Maya: yes — in Redwood Console you can pin eval sets and configure regression alerts. we'd suggest adding your core evals to console so alerts trigger automatically.
[03:06] Priya: on network peering — is VPN enough for private, or do we need cloud interconnect?
[03:12] Derek: VPN is supported but for predictable low-latency we recommend direct interconnect (e.g., aws direct connect). VPN variance is bigger.
[03:20] Alex: ok. about pricing/prorate — maya, will you email a sample invoice that shows how the mid-contract add-on is billed? our finance wants the exact prorate logic, not just estimates.
[03:32] Maya: yes, i'll produce a redlined amendment + example invoice showing prorate for commit increases mid-term. we'll include line items for dedicated baseline, burst pool, and apac region premium.
[03:45] Sam: for the bench, what config should derek run? our token mix: 70% short, 25% medium, 5% long. sequence length 40 median, p95 780.
[03:58] Derek: i'll configure a run with ptoken=64 default and a few tails at 1k seq to simulate p95. i'll also test KV cache hit vs miss. quick note — transcription/mic: KV cache often shows as K-V cash in auto transcripts, so sorry if the console smells funny.
[04:18] Alex: ha — noted. on region choice: we prefer SG for APAC, EU remains frankfurt. is there any limitation to staging the APAC cluster after EU?
[04:28] Derek: no, we can stage EU first then APAC; provisioning time for a private APAC cluster is ~3 weeks from contract signature depending on HSM integration and network approvals. hosted APAC is much faster (~3–5 days).
[04:42] Priya: our compliance team asks if Redwood stores any plaintext request logs outside our S3 — need assurance no PII is retained by default.
[04:51] Maya: default logs are metadata-only on our control plane; for Private we can disable retention and route logs to your bucket. we will include this in the security pack.
[05:05] Alex: great. let's recap next steps.

Recap & Next Steps (live):
- Derek to run throughput/latency micro-benchmark with provided prompt set and share raw numbers and a 1-page readout (due 2025-08-20).
- Maya to send commitment amendment + sample prorated invoice showing APAC uplift and burst pricing (due 2025-08-22).
- Sam to upload 1,000 anonymized example requests to secure link (due 2025-08-24).
- Priya to confirm APAC region and KMS/HSM preference (due 2025-08-25).

[05:40] Alex: that timeline looks good. one ask — can we get a simple TCO slide that compares hosted vs dedicated vs private (with KMS) for our monthly baseline and promotional peak?
[05:52] Maya: yes, i'll include that with the amendment.
[06:00] Priya: also please include the network pattern for peering and expected ip ranges so our network team can pre-approve.
[06:08] Derek: will include architecture snippet and a small checklist for on-prem HSM prep.
[06:18] Maya: ok wrapping up — i'll get docs out this week. thanks everyone.
[06:22] Alex: thanks all.

End transcript.
